headline: 14 killed, 30 injured in bus-truck collision in Natore
summary: A head-on collision between a sand-laden truck and a passenger bus on the Natore-Pabna highway claimed 14 lives and left dozens injured.
details: A devastating head-on collision between a passenger bus and a sand-laden truck occurred on the Natore-Pabna highway in front of the Bonpara Police Investigation Center in Natore's Boroigram upazila.
At least 14 people were killed in the crash, including nine who died on the spot and five others who succumbed to their injuries at various hospitals.

Among the victims were a father and his 8-year-old daughter, who were traveling to Rajshahi to spend the Puja holidays with relatives. The mother and 10-year-old son are currently receiving treatment in hospitals.
Five businessmen from Shariatpur's Jazira upazila were also among the dead, who were traveling to Bagmara in Rajshahi to purchase agricultural seeds and other products.
The victims included Jewel Madbor, Salal Molla, Saloh Shikdar, Abdus Samad Fakir, and Shahin Bepari. Two other businessmen from the same group were injured in the crash.
The victims' families have been contacted, and bodies are being processed for transfer to their respective hometowns for burial and final rites.
According to reports, the bus was an RP Special Transport bus heading toward Chapainawabganj from Borguna.

headline_marked: Dhaka courier office [[vandalised and looted over rent demand]]
headline: Dhaka courier office vandalised and looted over rent demand
summary: Over 100 people allegedly attacked the AJR Courier Service warehouse in Hazaribagh, demanding rent be paid to a listed criminal.
details: A group of more than 100 people allegedly vandalised and looted the AJR Courier Service office and warehouse in Dhaka’s Hazaribagh on Tuesday evening.
Masked men wearing helmets climbed over the boundary wall and threatened security guards after disabling CCTV cameras at nearby houses.
The attackers vandalised office furniture and looted laptops and goods, while also removing CCTV cameras and digital video recorders (DVRs) from the warehouse.
The group demanded that the company pay rent for the premises to Sanzidul Islam Emon, whom police have listed as a criminal.
AJR Courier Service stated they had a lease agreement with the Sikder Group and had been paying rent to them, but the attackers claimed rent should now be paid to Emon.
The attackers threatened that the company would not be allowed to operate unless the demand was met, and operations have remained suspended since the attack.
Hazaribagh Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mosharraf Hossain confirmed the incident, stating that police brought the situation under control.
As of Tuesday night, no one has been detained and no formal complaint or case has been filed over the incident.
caption:
Over 100 people, including masked men in helmets, stormed a Dhaka courier office to demand rent for a listed criminal.

A group of more than 100 people allegedly vandalised and looted the AJR Courier Service office and warehouse in Dhaka’s Hazaribagh on Tuesday evening.

Masked men wearing helmets climbed over the boundary wall and threatened security guards after disabling CCTV cameras at nearby houses.

The attackers vandalised office furniture and looted laptops and goods, while also removing CCTV cameras and digital video recorders (DVRs) from the warehouse.

The group demanded that the company pay rent for the premises to Sanzidul Islam Emon, whom police have listed as a criminal.

AJR Courier Service stated they had a lease agreement with the Sikder Group and had been paying rent to them, but the attackers claimed rent should now be paid to Emon.

The attackers threatened that the company would not be allowed to operate unless the demand was met, and operations have remained suspended since the attack.

Hazaribagh Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mosharraf Hossain confirmed the incident, stating that police brought the situation under control.

As of Tuesday night, no one has been detained and no formal complaint or case has been filed over the incident.
